key_insight: A dynamically stabilized hexagonal ZrO interlayer emerges as a significant oxygen diffusion barrier while simulations reproduce columnar zirconium corrosion films.
engineering_relevance: The model links oxide microstructure, oxygen transport, and local tensile stresses to mechanisms relevant to corrosion resistance and crack initiation.
method: Compute ZrOₓ properties using first-principles density functional theory.
Use a DFT-trained machine-learned potential for molecular dynamics inputs.
Simulate oxide growth with multiphase phase-field modeling of nucleation, diffusion, elasticity, and phase stability.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports agreement with observed columnar film morphology and grain size distributions, plus reproduction of an undulating metal/oxide interface.
watch_item: The abstract provides no quantitative validation errors; the proposed ZrO contribution to sub-parabolic corrosion kinetics remains tentative.
paper_title: Multiscale Modeling of Zr Corrosion: Predicting Microstructures of Oxide Films
